Law.name: {=BC_GenderLaw_MaleOnly}Male Only
Law.description: {=BC_GenderLaw_MaleOnly_Desc}Only men may inherit. If the house is left without any man, its lands and titles revert to the crown while the surviving house retains strong claims.

Law.name: {=BC_GenderLaw_MalePreference}Male Preference
Law.description: {=BC_GenderLaw_MalePreference_Desc}Men take precedence over women of the same dynastic standing.

Law.name: {=BC_GenderLaw_Equal}Equal
Law.description: {=BC_GenderLaw_Equal_Desc}Gender carries no weight in the line of succession.

Law.name: {=BC_GenderLaw_FemalePreference}Female Preference
Law.description: {=BC_GenderLaw_FemalePreference_Desc}Women take precedence over men of the same dynastic standing.

Law.name: {=BC_GenderLaw_FemaleOnly}Female Only
Law.description: {=BC_GenderLaw_FemaleOnly_Desc}Only women may inherit. If the house is left without any woman, its lands and titles revert to the crown while the surviving house retains strong claims.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Primogeniture}Primogeniture
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Primogeniture_Desc}The eldest child's branch inherits first, with descendants representing a deceased ancestor.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Ultimogeniture}Ultimogeniture
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Ultimogeniture_Desc}The youngest child's branch inherits first, with descendants representing a deceased ancestor.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_ElectiveSeniority}Elective Seniority
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_ElectiveSeniority_Desc}Realm elections favor adult experience, leadership, stewardship and charm. Blood ties confer a small advantage but are not required.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Seniority}Seniority
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Seniority_Desc}The oldest eligible blood relative inherits the Crown, with the preferred gender taking precedence where the gender law requires it. Clan membership does not determine Crown rights.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_MilitaryAcclamation}Military Acclamation
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_MilitaryAcclamation_Desc}Realm elections favor leadership, tactics, martial ability and active command of a party or army.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Tanistry}Tanistry
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Tanistry_Desc}Realm elections strongly favor clan leaders related to the ruler within four generations, alongside leadership and martial merit. Unrelated clan leaders remain eligible.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_ShuraCouncil}Shura Council
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_ShuraCouncil_Desc}Realm elections favor stewardship, charm, leadership, trade, adult experience and current service as a governor.

Law.name: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Kinship}Kinship
Law.description: {=BC_SuccessionLaw_Kinship_Desc}Blood relatives within four generations compete through kinship, leadership, charm, stewardship and tactics. The highest-ranked lawful heir inherits the Crown directly; no succession vote is held unless no valid heir remains.

Law.name: {=BC_Term_OneYear}1 year
Law.description: {=BC_Term_OneYear_Desc}Each elected sovereign receives a one-year mandate. Reforms also affect the sitting ruler: fixed terms retain their original start, while a lifetime mandate converted to a fixed term begins upon adoption. An overdue term leads to an election after deliberation.

Law.name: {=BC_Term_FiveYears}5 years
Law.description: {=BC_Term_FiveYears_Desc}Each elected sovereign receives a five-year mandate. Reforms also affect the sitting ruler: fixed terms retain their original start, while a lifetime mandate converted to a fixed term begins upon adoption. An overdue term leads to an election after deliberation.

Law.name: {=BC_Term_TenYears}10 years
Law.description: {=BC_Term_TenYears_Desc}Each elected sovereign receives a ten-year mandate. Reforms also affect the sitting ruler: fixed terms retain their original start, while a lifetime mandate converted to a fixed term begins upon adoption. An overdue term leads to an election after deliberation.

Law.name: {=BC_Term_Lifetime}Lifetime mandate
Law.description: {=BC_Term_Lifetime_Desc}Each elected sovereign serves for life or until abdication. Reforms also affect the sitting ruler: fixed terms retain their original start, while a lifetime mandate converted to a fixed term begins upon adoption. An overdue term leads to an election after deliberation.
